chunks: Al-Washshāʾ narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A man from among my companions has sent me news that he is coming from Al-Aʿwaṣ, and that is during the month of Ramadan. Shall I go to meet him and break my fast?” He said: “Yes.”
I said: “Shall I go to meet him and break my fast, or remain and fast?” He said: “Go to meet him and break your fast.”

key_terms.أَتَلَقَّاهُ: shall I go out to meet him; referring to setting out to receive the arriving companion
key_terms.أَصُومُ: I fast; meaning to continue the Ramadan fast while staying resident
key_terms.أُفْطِرُ: I break my fast; meaning to refrain from continuing the obligatory fast due to travel
key_terms.أُقِيمُ: I remain in place; meaning not to travel
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time in which the ruling is being asked about

ai.seo_question: Can a person travel to meet someone during Ramadan and break the fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning travel in the month of Ramadan. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام permits going out to meet a companion arriving from another place, even when that entails breaking the fast due to travel.
